question: A junior engineer proposes capping an autonomous research agent at exactly 5 tool-call iterations and treating that cap as the loop's primary stopping mechanism, regardless of stop_reason. What is the main architectural problem with relying on a fixed iteration cap this way?
options: A) It causes the API to immediately reject the request, since the Messages API enforces its own hard limit of five tool calls total
B) It can cut the loop off while stop_reason is still "tool_use", forcing the agent to abandon work Claude has not finished reasoning through
C) It forces every one of the later requests to omit the tools parameter entirely, disabling any further tool use for the rest of that session
D) It stops tool_result blocks from being appended to conversation history entirely once the third iteration has completed
correct_answers: B) It can cut the loop off while stop_reason is still "tool_use", forcing the agent to abandon work Claude has not finished reasoning through
explanations: Incorrect. The Messages API has no built-in limit on tool calls per conversation; any cap is an application-level choice.

Correct. An iteration cap is arbitrary and unrelated to task completion, so using it as the primary stop condition can truncate the loop mid-task; termination should instead follow stop_reason == "end_turn".
Incorrect. Reaching an iteration cap only affects whether the loop sends another request; it does not alter the tools parameter of any request.
Incorrect. Appending tool_result blocks is a client-side responsibility that has nothing to do with any iteration counter the loop maintains.
